chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffi said: Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Bahrani, who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: The five who cried are: Adam, Jacob, Joseph, Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them all). As for Adam, he cried over Paradise until his cheeks became like valleys. As for Jacob, he cried over Joseph until his sight was lost, and it was said to him: 'By Allah, you will ceaselessly remember Joseph until you become consumptive with grief or perish.' As for Joseph, he cried over Jacob until the people of the prison were bothered by him, so they said to him: 'Either cry at night and be silent by day, or cry by day and be silent at night.' He made a compromise with them on one of the two. As for Fatimah, she cried over the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) until the people of Medina were bothered by her, so they said to her: 'You have annoyed us with your frequent crying.' So she would go out to the graveyards, the graveyards of the martyrs, and cry until she fulfilled her need, then she would return. As for Ali ibn al-Husayn, he cried over al-Husayn (peace be upon him) for twenty or forty years; whenever food was placed before him, he would cry, until a servant of his said to him: 'I am your ransom, O son of the Messenger of Allah! I fear that you may perish.' He said: 'I complain only of my distress and sorrow to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know.' I do not remember the martyrdom of the children of Fatimah but that tears choke me because of it.

key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ: Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin, peace be upon him)
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ مُحَمَّدٍ: Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon her)

ai.seo_question: Who are the five people known for their weeping in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these five figures to establish a spiritual lineage of grief, culminating in the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby elevating weeping from mere emotion to a devotional act of remembrance (dhikr). The narrative specifically links the prolonged mourning of Fatimah and Ali ibn al-Husayn to the concept of 'Bath' (deep sorrow) mentioned in Surah Yusuf, illustrating how their tears served as a testament to their unique connection with the Divine.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-15 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Bahrani who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “There are five who cried: Adam (MGB); Jacob (MGB); Joseph (MGB); Fatimah - the daughter of Muhammad (MGB); and Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB).”

Adam (MGB) cried over Paradise so much that his tears flowed like a creek on his face.Jacob (MGB) cried for Joseph (MGB) so much that he became blind and he was told, ‘By Allah. (never) wilt thou cease to remember Joseph until thou reach the last extremity of illness, or until thou die!’And Joseph (MGB) cried for Jacob (MGB) so much in the prison that the other prisoners asked him to either cry in the daytime or at night. He (MGB) accepted and only cried once every twenty-four hours.And Fatimah (MGB) cried over God’s Prophet (MGB) so much that the residents of Medina got upset and told her that her crying is bothering them. Then she left the town every day and went to the graveyards of the martyrs, where she cried and then she returned. Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB) cried over Al-Hussein (MGB) for twenty of forty years. He (MGB) cried whenever he wanted to eat or drink until his servant told him, “O (grand)son of God’s Prophet! May I be your ransom! I fear that you may perish!’ As-Sajjad replied, ‘I shall take my sorrow and complaint to God. I know what you do not know. Whenever I remember the martyrdom of the children of Fatimah (MGB) I cry.’
